title: Experimental expansion blueprint
status: planning-only; no question JSON or live bank changes
purpose: Coverage plan for 100 additional experimental scenario briefs toward a 1,000-question expansion. Each brief is a candidate scene, not an approved answer key.
coverageGaps: Existing content heavily repeats scan/support/retrieval freezes; add first-touch, puck-protection, deception, escape and recovery choices with changed cues.
U7 needs more one-player-at-a-time movement, balance, stop/start and simple puck-owner recognition without multi-player systems.
U9 needs half-ice decision variety: carry-versus-pass, support distance, direction change, restart awareness and simple role flexibility.
U11 needs the widest fundamentals-to-game bridge: escapes, gap changes, lane creation, possession quality, third-player support and conditional role swaps.
U13 needs open-ended time/space reads, transition choices, weak-side awareness and flexible responsibilities beyond the existing breakout/entry set.
U15/U18 need more context-sensitive puck management and communication, while special-teams material remains explicitly system-scoped.
Paid Hockey Tactics material is inspiration only; no row relies on unseen book content or a precise universal rule.

sourcePlan.boundary: Sources support topic placement and bounded principles only. Final cues, geometry, timing, alternatives and answer logic require the tactical, physics and coaching review gates.

briefs.title: Stop before the loose puck
briefs.objective: Recognize a controlled stop before reaching a loose puck.
briefs.context: Cross-ice practice; one child approaches a puck with a clear stopping marker.
briefs.cue: Puck is still loose; coach has named the stopping marker.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds stop-before-approach sequencing; existing U7 covers loose-puck recognition without a movement-control choice.

briefs.title: Turn toward the open gate
briefs.objective: Choose a visible turn toward open space while carrying slowly.
briefs.context: Small-ice lane with one blocked gate and one open gate.
briefs.cue: The first route is occupied; the open gate is clearly marked.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Tests turning direction during a carry; existing open-space carry asks only which route has room.

briefs.title: Pass to the ready partner
briefs.objective: Identify the partner who is facing the puck and ready for a short pass.
briefs.context: Two partners are shown, one facing away and one presenting a stick.
briefs.cue: Only one receiver has a visible ready target.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds receiver-read detail; existing beginner receiving identifies a general invited receiver.

briefs.title: Keep the puck beside you
briefs.objective: Choose a carry line that keeps the puck within a simple reachable path.
briefs.context: Beginner carry with a wide safe lane and a board-side obstacle.
briefs.cue: The puck starts beside the stick; the obstacle narrows one route.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Focuses puck distance during movement; existing U7 carry asks about room, not control relationship.

briefs.title: Back up to see the puck
briefs.objective: Recognize backward movement that keeps the play in view.
briefs.context: A child backs toward a marked line while a partner carries forward.
briefs.cue: The player must see the carrier while moving back.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Introduces movement-direction observation; existing scan-behind is stationary teammate recognition.

briefs.title: Choose the shorter safe pass
briefs.objective: Select the clearly open short pass rather than the crossed occupied lane.
briefs.context: Two-player cross-ice practice with one obvious defender marker.
briefs.cue: One lane is visibly clear and one is visibly occupied.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds simple lane choice; existing U7 pass content centers on ownership and receiver identity.

briefs.title: Freeze the puck for the restart
briefs.objective: Recognize the coach-designated freeze and move to the named restart spot.
briefs.context: Declared cross-ice practice model with a goalie-freeze illustration.
briefs.cue: The puck is covered and the restart marker is named.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds restart-location recognition; existing rotating-goal and practice-stop scenes do not connect freeze to restart.

briefs.title: Leave space for your partner
briefs.objective: Choose a spot that leaves a visible lane for a partner.
briefs.context: Two children share a small-ice lane; one is carrying and one is supporting.
briefs.cue: Standing directly beside the carrier blocks the simple lane.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Introduces spacing as availability; existing after-pass role assumes the pass already happened.

briefs.title: Slow down at the circle
briefs.objective: Match a slower approach to a marked turn area.
briefs.context: A skating path has a straight section and a marked circle turn.
briefs.cue: The turn is near; the child is still moving quickly.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Links speed choice to a landmark; existing rink-landmark reset is a location instruction without movement control.

briefs.title: Try again with the puck loose
briefs.objective: Recognize the next helpful action after a missed pass leaves the puck loose.
briefs.context: Partner pass misses by a short distance in a calm practice lane.
briefs.cue: No player owns the puck after the miss.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Separates mistake recovery from team reassurance; existing reset-after-mistake does not require a new puck action.

briefs.title: Carry past the first marker
briefs.objective: Choose a carry when the near lane is open and support is not yet ready.
briefs.context: Half-ice lane with a passive marker and a partner arriving late.
briefs.cue: The carrier has room for one controlled touch before the marker.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds timing between carry and pass; existing board-side control does not compare a late receiver.

briefs.title: Pass before the lane closes
briefs.objective: Notice a clear lane that is about to be occupied and choose the timely pass.
briefs.context: Half-ice 2v1-style teaching picture with no scoring claim.
briefs.cue: The passing lane is open now; a defender marker is moving toward it.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds when-to-pass timing; existing closed-pass lane is already blocked at the freeze.

briefs.title: Protect the puck on the outside
briefs.objective: Choose the side of the body that keeps the puck farther from pressure.
briefs.context: Half-ice carry beside a board with pressure on one shoulder.
briefs.cue: Pressure comes from the inside, while the outside lane remains available.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds body-side puck protection; existing board-side control identifies pressure without a side-choice branch.

briefs.title: Change direction after the touch
briefs.objective: Select a change of direction after the first touch opens a new lane.
briefs.context: Small-area carry with one defender marker and two exit gates.
briefs.cue: The defender follows the initial route, leaving the second gate open.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Uses a defender response to create the choice; existing turn-before-traffic is U11 and pre-traffic.

briefs.title: Support below the puck
briefs.objective: Choose a lower support spot that gives the carrier a safe reset lane.
briefs.context: Half-ice puck carrier near the wall with a teammate above and below.
briefs.cue: The upper support is covered; the lower lane is visible.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds vertical support choice; existing near-far support compares distance rather than below/above relationship.

briefs.title: Move after your pass
briefs.objective: Reposition into a new lane after a completed pass.
briefs.context: Two-player half-ice give-and-go with a third marker occupying the original spot.
briefs.cue: The partner now owns the puck; the passer’s old spot is covered.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds post-pass relocation; existing give-and-go window focuses on a return angle near a circle.

briefs.title: Recover the pass that skips
briefs.objective: Update from receiving to recovery when a pass misses behind the target.
briefs.context: Half-ice pass travels beyond the intended receiver with no secure owner.
briefs.cue: The puck is loose and the original receiver is nearest, but pressure approaches.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds direction-of-miss recovery; existing blocked-pass loose puck is a defender block, not an overrun pass.

briefs.title: Use the open side of the circle
briefs.objective: Choose a receiving or carry route on the less crowded side of a faceoff circle.
briefs.context: Half-ice circle with one teammate and one opponent occupying the near side.
briefs.cue: The far arc has room and remains inside the declared practice area.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds curved-landmark space reading; existing circle scene is a return-pass angle.

briefs.title: Wait for the receiver to face you
briefs.objective: Recognize that an intended receiver is not ready until facing the puck.
briefs.context: Half-ice pass setup with two teammates in different orientations.
briefs.cue: One player is stationary but facing away; the other presents a target.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds receiver orientation; existing wall reception focuses on pressure side.

briefs.title: Reset when the coach calls change
briefs.objective: Follow the explicitly named half-ice change sequence after the signal.
briefs.context: Declared U9 half-ice model; puck carrier receives the change cue.
briefs.cue: Coach signal and model are stated before the scene.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds event ordering after a change signal; existing half-ice shift-change scene recognizes the signal without a puck-carrier decision.

briefs.title: Make room after a goalie freeze
briefs.objective: Choose a safe support space after the scoped goalie restart.
briefs.context: Declared half-ice goalie-freeze restart with teammates returning to marked lanes.
briefs.cue: The puck is covered and the restart instruction is visible.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds post-restart spacing; existing goalie-restart scene identifies possession and room without a new lane choice.

briefs.title: Shield before you turn
briefs.objective: Choose a turn that keeps the puck on the side away from a marker.
briefs.context: Half-ice receive with pressure arriving from behind one shoulder.
briefs.cue: The inside turn leads toward pressure; the outside turn has space.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds turn-side protection; existing receive-rescan ends at awareness after reception.

briefs.title: See the second teammate
briefs.objective: Find the teammate who becomes available after the first option is covered.
briefs.context: Carrier has a near receiver and a second teammate across the lane.
briefs.cue: The near receiver is marked; the far teammate is visible in open space.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds second-option scan after a coverage change; existing support-under-double-pressure is pressure concentration at the puck.

briefs.title: Stop the carry at the boundary
briefs.objective: Recognize the named half-ice boundary before carrying beyond it.
briefs.context: Coach labels the playable lane and a restart boundary.
briefs.cue: The puck and player approach the marked boundary together.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds boundary-aware puck management; existing landmark reset uses boards/circle rather than a play-area edge.

briefs.title: Follow the puck after a tip
briefs.objective: Track the new puck direction after an explicit deflection.
briefs.context: Half-ice pass touches a stick and changes angle; no player is credited with control yet.
briefs.cue: The puck’s new path differs from the intended pass.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds changed puck trajectory; existing loose-puck scenes use static ownership or blocked lanes.

briefs.title: Escape to the backhand side
briefs.objective: Compare escape sides after locating pressure on the forehand side.
briefs.context: Defensive-zone retrieval with one forechecker and two explicitly drawn exits.
briefs.cue: Pressure closes the first side; the far-side exit retains space.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds escape-side comparison; existing U11 retrieval asks about scanning before planning.

briefs.title: Reverse before the wall closes
briefs.objective: Recognize when a reverse option becomes useful as the first route closes.
briefs.context: Corner retrieval with a partner arriving behind the net.
briefs.cue: The original wall outlet is occupied; the reverse lane is visible and declared.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds timing of a reverse; existing U13 breakout-reverse is a higher-band outlet-close scene.

briefs.title: Bump the puck into space
briefs.objective: Choose a controlled bump into open ice when carrying space is narrow.
briefs.context: Defensive-zone wall pressure with a safe, visible space behind the pressure.
briefs.cue: The puck cannot be carried through the pressure without losing separation.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds bump-versus-carry management; existing indirect-pass uses a half-wall route rather than a pressure escape.

briefs.title: Delay until support arrives
briefs.objective: Hold a protected puck briefly when the forward option is not yet available.
briefs.context: Regroup with a carrier, one covered option and a teammate arriving underneath.
briefs.cue: No immediate pass is clearly open; support is becoming available.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds deliberate delay; existing change-of-pace asks whether to carry into room.

briefs.title: Use the middle after the first defender commits
briefs.objective: Identify the middle lane created when a defender follows the wide carrier.
briefs.context: Neutral-zone 2v1 teaching freeze with a stated no-guaranteed-shot outcome.
briefs.cue: The defender’s body position removes the wide route and opens inside space.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds defender-commitment lane creation; existing two-on-one read compares options without this explicit movement trigger.

briefs.title: Support the carrier’s escape
briefs.objective: Choose a support line that appears where the carrier can safely exit.
briefs.context: One carrier turns away from pressure while two teammates occupy different heights.
briefs.cue: The carrier’s escape side changes after the defender closes.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Makes support conditional on escape side; existing pass-and-support assumes a completed pass.

briefs.title: Close the gap without chasing
briefs.objective: Adjust approach pace while keeping the attacker in front.
briefs.context: Rush defense with a carrier changing speed and a declared protected middle.
briefs.cue: The carrier slows; the defender must avoid over-skating the play.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds pace response to gap control; existing inside-gap is a static relationship.

briefs.title: Angle the first touch wide
briefs.objective: Choose a first-touch direction that moves the carrier away from the middle.
briefs.context: 1v1 neutral-zone entry with an open wall lane and a protected slot.
briefs.cue: The carrier receives facing the middle; the defender has inside position.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Combines first touch with defensive angle; existing wide-angling begins after the carrier is already moving.

briefs.title: Read the puck’s bounce
briefs.objective: Separate a playable bounce from a puck that remains contested.
briefs.context: Wall puck changes direction off a board seam; two players approach.
briefs.cue: The puck’s next owner is not established by proximity alone.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds bounce interpretation; existing contested-possession uses a teammate near a stationary loose puck.

briefs.title: Choose the safer exit lane
briefs.objective: Compare a short covered outlet with a longer visibly open outlet.
briefs.context: Defender has possession below the goal line and two support options.
briefs.cue: The short pass lane contains a defender stick; the longer lane is open in the freeze.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds risk-distance tradeoff; existing reset-support is a behind-carrier outlet without explicit lane contrast.

briefs.title: Replace the vacated support
briefs.objective: Move into the space left when a teammate leaves to receive.
briefs.context: Three-player breakout with one high support spot and a teammate dropping low.
briefs.cue: The original support lane is now empty and useful.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds replacement movement; existing after-pass role follows a completed pass, not a teammate’s movement.

briefs.title: Hold the middle on a turnover
briefs.objective: Recognize the first defensive space to protect after an explicit turnover.
briefs.context: Neutral-zone turnover with a puck carrier wide and a second attacker inside.
briefs.cue: Possession changes; the middle lane is the immediate threat cue.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds priority after turnover; existing turnover-transition changes jobs without a specific middle-space cue.

briefs.title: Recover behind the play
briefs.objective: Choose a recovery route that reaches useful middle ice rather than following the puck wide.
briefs.context: A missed offensive challenge leaves two opposing lanes.
briefs.cue: The puck carrier is wide; another attacker is inside the route to goal.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds route selection after a missed challenge; existing defensive-recovery is a generic job change.

briefs.title: Open a lane with a give
briefs.objective: Recognize the new lane created by passing and moving away from the defender.
briefs.context: Small-area give-and-go with one defender following the passer.
briefs.cue: The return lane opens only after the passer changes angle.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds defender-response give-and-go; existing give-and-go material is U13 and near a fixed landmark.

briefs.title: Shoot around the first blocker
briefs.objective: Choose a small lateral adjustment that changes the visible shooting lane.
briefs.context: Point-area shot picture with a blocker and an open adjacent lane.
briefs.cue: The first shot line is covered; the adjacent line remains visible.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds lateral shot adjustment; existing slot-shot-lane only identifies a separate pass option.

briefs.title: Attack the rebound side
briefs.objective: Choose a route to the visible loose-puck side after a save.
briefs.context: Shot and rebound freeze with the puck loose and two players approaching.
briefs.cue: The puck is not controlled; one route is blocked by a defender.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds rebound-side route choice; existing rebound-awareness only separates loose from promised rebound.

briefs.title: Support the second touch
briefs.objective: Choose a position that helps after a teammate’s first wall touch.
briefs.context: Wall battle with a visible second touch option inside.
briefs.cue: The first player may not secure possession on contact-free static illustration.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds second-touch anticipation; existing corner-role separation is retrieval-versus-support at the first contest.

briefs.title: Keep the far option visible
briefs.objective: Scan the far-side teammate before committing to a puck-side move.
briefs.context: Offensive-zone puck carrier with a crowded near side and open far-side support.
briefs.cue: The near lane contains two bodies; the far teammate is visible.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds far-side commitment check; existing cross-ice support is U13 and centered on a half-wall comparison.

briefs.title: Keep a route home after joining
briefs.objective: Choose an activation that preserves a route back if possession is lost.
briefs.context: Defender considers joining a rush while a partner remains behind.
briefs.cue: The covering teammate and a return lane are explicitly shown.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds activation exit condition; existing role-switch and defender activation are older-band concepts.

briefs.title: Use the wall as a reset
briefs.objective: Recognize a wall pass as a reset option when the middle is covered.
briefs.context: Carrier near the wall, middle defender set, partner available along the boards.
briefs.cue: The middle route is closed; the wall route is visibly open.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds wall-reset purpose; existing indirect-pass changes route but does not make the middle closure the trigger.

briefs.title: Re-scan after the defender bites
briefs.objective: Update the next action when a defender leaves the original lane to pressure.
briefs.context: Carrier receives with two options; defender shifts toward the first option.
briefs.cue: The defender’s movement changes which lane is available.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds a defender-bite trigger; existing receive-scan is before reception and receive-rescan is U9 after reception.

briefs.title: Choose a support height
briefs.objective: Compare low, middle and high support against the carrier’s pressure and direction.
briefs.context: Three support heights are shown in a neutral-zone regroup.
briefs.cue: The carrier faces pressure from one side and needs an available outlet.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds vertical-height selection; existing centre-low and high-forward support belong to U13.

briefs.title: Protect possession during a change
briefs.objective: Choose a support action that preserves possession while a teammate changes.
briefs.context: Declared practice substitution with one carrier and one changing teammate.
briefs.cue: The carrier has a safe hold lane and a risky forced pass lane.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds change-window possession choice; existing line-change puck management is U15 and full context.

briefs.title: Delay the shot for a lane
briefs.objective: Recognize when one touch can improve a covered shot lane.
briefs.context: Carrier at the point with a teammate occupying the first lane.
briefs.cue: A small lateral touch opens a second lane while pressure remains manageable.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds shot timing; existing slot-shot-lane is a static blocked line.

briefs.title: Name the job that changed
briefs.objective: Identify the current role after an explicit puck and player movement change.
briefs.context: Three-player transition where the planned receiver becomes the carrier.
briefs.cue: The puck owner changes and the original carrier moves into support.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Tests flexible role reassignment; existing after-pass and turnover-transition each cover only one fixed change.

briefs.title: Exit pressure with a shoulder check
briefs.objective: Use a second pressure check after the first retrieval lane changes.
briefs.context: Defensive-zone retrieval with forechecker route changing behind the net.
briefs.cue: The first scan is stale because the forechecker changes side.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds repeated scan under changing pressure; existing breakout retrieval is a single pre-rim read.

briefs.title: Escape before the second forechecker arrives
briefs.objective: Compare an immediate safe outlet with waiting for a preferred lane that is closing.
briefs.context: Two-forechecker breakout freeze with one lane open now.
briefs.cue: The preferred outlet is farther away and a second defender is arriving.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds time-window tradeoff; existing reverse and wall-support scenes use one pressure cue.

briefs.title: Carry behind the forechecker
briefs.objective: Recognize the space created when a forechecker overskates the carrier.
briefs.context: Breakout carrier turns up ice after a forechecker commits below the puck.
briefs.cue: The forechecker’s momentum leaves a visible lane behind the pressure.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds pressure manipulation by carry; existing puck-protection scenes focus on keeping away from a nearby defender.

briefs.title: Use the late middle option
briefs.objective: Choose a middle support lane that appears after the first entry option is denied.
briefs.context: Neutral-zone regroup with a wide carrier and a delayed middle player.
briefs.cue: The wide lane is pressured; the middle player arrives behind the play.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds delayed support after denial; existing middle-support scene is a static underneath option.

briefs.title: Change the entry point
briefs.objective: Update an entry route when the original lane is sealed.
briefs.context: Wide entry with a second lane across the blue line and no universal offside claim.
briefs.cue: The defender closes the first lane before the carrier crosses.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds pre-entry lane switching; existing wide-entry support assumes the route remains.

briefs.title: Delay instead of forcing the rim
briefs.objective: Choose a delay when the immediate entry is covered and support is regrouping.
briefs.context: Carrier near the blue line with two covered forward routes.
briefs.cue: A trailing teammate is becoming available behind the carrier.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds delay as possession protection; existing entry-delay timing tests arrival timing rather than the carrier’s choice.

briefs.title: Replace the middle after the pass
briefs.objective: Fill the middle lane after the original middle player moves to receive.
briefs.context: Three-player entry with an explicitly changing receiver and support role.
briefs.cue: The middle lane becomes empty after the pass.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds role replacement during entry; existing give-and-go is a short post-pass movement without lane ownership.

briefs.title: Keep the puck below the pressure
briefs.objective: Choose a low-zone hold or support route when the slot is crowded.
briefs.context: Offensive-zone carrier below the goal line with a crowded slot.
briefs.cue: A low support lane remains available while the slot is occupied.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds low-zone patience; existing offensive-possession reset is U15 and compares slot with low support.

briefs.title: Find the far-side seam
briefs.objective: Identify a far-side seam created by puck-side pressure.
briefs.context: Offensive-zone half-wall carrier with a far-side teammate and low defender.
briefs.cue: Two defenders lean toward the puck side; the far seam is visible.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds seam recognition under overload; existing weak-side coverage is defensive low-slot awareness.

briefs.title: Screen without losing the escape
briefs.objective: Choose a useful screen position that preserves a recovery route.
briefs.context: Point shot setup with a changing screen and a defender nearby.
briefs.cue: The screen lane is useful only if the player can recover when the puck moves.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds screen-to-recovery flexibility; existing net-front recognition avoids contested positioning technique.

briefs.title: Pass around the active stick
briefs.objective: Choose a pass lane that avoids a defender’s active stick while retaining support.
briefs.context: Half-wall carrier with a defender stick shading the direct lane.
briefs.cue: The defender’s stick blocks one line; a short angle around it is open.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds stick-lane read; existing shooting-lane addresses a shot blocker rather than a pass lane.

briefs.title: Receive on the safe shoulder
briefs.objective: Choose a receiving side that lets the player see pressure and next support.
briefs.context: Pass arrives with a defender on one shoulder and a teammate on the other side.
briefs.cue: The receiver can angle the first touch to one of two sides.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds first-touch side selection; existing receiving-control asks whether to settle before acting.

briefs.title: Keep one player above the puck
briefs.objective: Recognize the support height that protects against a counterattack.
briefs.context: Two teammates attack low while a third chooses a higher support lane.
briefs.cue: Both low players are below the puck; one high lane is open.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds counterattack balance; existing high-forward-support is a static recognition scene.

briefs.title: Change from forecheck to reload
briefs.objective: Recognize when the first forecheck is no longer supported and reload instead.
briefs.context: Carrier escapes the wall and the closest forechecker is behind the play.
briefs.cue: The puck exits pressure; a second attacker is visible up ice.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds forecheck-to-reload transition; existing backcheck-recovery begins after a defensive recovery route.

briefs.title: Protect the inside on a switch
briefs.objective: Exchange pressure with a teammate while retaining inside position.
briefs.context: Two defenders face a carrier and a supporting attacker crossing lanes.
briefs.cue: The switch is explicitly called; the inside threat remains visible.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds communicated switch with inside retention; existing defensive-zone support avoids duplicating pressure without a lane exchange.

briefs.title: Track the second attacker after the pass
briefs.objective: Choose a tracking line after the puck moves to a new attacker.
briefs.context: Transition pass changes the carrier while a second attacker cuts inside.
briefs.cue: The original carrier is no longer the puck threat.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds post-pass threat update; existing possession-switch is a static turnover change.

briefs.title: Hold the line, then retreat
briefs.objective: Choose between holding a line and retreating when support is uncertain.
briefs.context: Neutral-zone defender has a carrier approaching and a partner’s location explicitly shown.
briefs.cue: The partner may be late; the carrier has a wide escape lane.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds conditional line judgment; existing gap-control is a receive-the-rush freeze.

briefs.title: Move the puck before the pinch
briefs.objective: Recognize a quick puck movement that beats a supported pinch.
briefs.context: Offensive blue-line puck with an explicitly declared covering teammate.
briefs.cue: The pinching defender commits while the wall carrier has a safe outlet.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds response to a pinch; existing U15 supported-pinch evaluates the defender’s decision.

briefs.title: Choose the second rebound job
briefs.objective: Select a distinct role after a teammate reaches the first rebound.
briefs.context: Shot rebound with one player attacking the puck and another choosing support.
briefs.cue: The first rebound player’s route is explicit; the second job remains open.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds second-player rebound role; existing rebound-response focuses on locating the rebound.

briefs.title: Reset behind a crowded slot
briefs.objective: Choose a reset lane when the immediate slot option is occupied.
briefs.context: Offensive-zone carrier with covered slot and open point-side support.
briefs.cue: The slot has bodies; the carrier can retain possession and move it back out.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds reset from crowding; existing shooting-lane only compares point angles.

briefs.title: Change the support job after a rim
briefs.objective: Update from expected receiver to retrieval support after a puck is rimmed.
briefs.context: Breakout rim changes the likely first toucher and support lanes.
briefs.cue: The puck travels farther than the original receiving point.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds role change caused by puck travel; existing breakout scenes assume the retrieval target.

briefs.title: Carry until the support is level
briefs.objective: Use a controlled carry while waiting for a support player to become level.
briefs.context: Neutral-zone carrier with a trailing teammate and a defender shading the pass.
briefs.cue: The pass is possible only after support reaches a usable angle.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds level-support timing; existing entry-delay timing is an arrival-after-delay scene.

briefs.title: Read the goalie’s set position
briefs.objective: Compare a shot lane with a pass lane after the goalie’s position is shown.
briefs.context: Offensive-zone carrier has a screened lane and a visible teammate.
briefs.cue: The goalie’s angle removes one shot option but does not prove a goal outcome.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds goalie cue to shot/pass choice; existing point-shot traffic uses changing screens only.

briefs.title: Recover the middle after a failed pinch
briefs.objective: Choose a recovery route after the pinch does not gain possession.
briefs.context: Blue-line activation fails and the opponent exits wide with an inside option.
briefs.cue: Possession is explicitly lost; the inside route is the nearer danger.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds failed-pinch recovery; existing backcheck-recovery is a forward’s route, not blue-line activation.

briefs.title: Pass, then cover the vacated lane
briefs.objective: Change to a defensive cover after a pass is intercepted.
briefs.context: A planned offensive pass is explicitly intercepted; two lanes open behind the play.
briefs.cue: The former passer is closest to one recovery lane; a teammate covers the other.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds immediate cover assignment after interception; existing possession-switch simply recognizes the turnover.

briefs.title: Manage the puck before the change
briefs.objective: Choose a low-risk possession action while a teammate changes.
briefs.context: Five-player-style schematic with a declared substitution and two support options.
briefs.cue: A forced central pass is covered; a protected hold or wall reset is available.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds decision comparison during a change; existing line-change management is a single-scene protected-possession prompt.

briefs.title: Use the middle after the penalty kill shifts
briefs.objective: Recognize the newly available middle lane after a declared flank shift.
briefs.context: Scoped penalty-kill shape with the protected slot stated.
briefs.cue: The puck moves flank; one defender shifts and another lane opens.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds exploiting a shifted lane; existing penalty-kill shift prioritizes remembering the slot.

briefs.title: Delay the power-play entry
briefs.objective: Choose a delay when the first entry lane is covered and support is arriving.
briefs.context: Scoped five-on-four entry with a carrier, trailer and defender lane.
briefs.cue: The direct entry is closed; a controlled regroup option remains.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds power-play entry patience; existing PP rush entry is U18 and asks whether a rush option exists.

briefs.title: Read the first touch after a draw
briefs.objective: Choose the next support job after the planned faceoff touch is redirected.
briefs.context: Scoped special-teams draw with the intended first touch and two outcomes shown.
briefs.cue: The puck travels to a different lane than the planned win.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds redirected first-touch contingency; existing power-play faceoff recovery separates retrieval from formation.

briefs.title: Keep the third player useful
briefs.objective: Choose a third-player height that supports both possession and defensive recovery.
briefs.context: Neutral-zone transition with two active players and a third choosing a lane.
briefs.cue: The puck carrier may continue or lose possession; both outcomes are visible.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds third-player dual-outcome support; existing role exchange is a declared swap.

briefs.title: Use a soft-area escape
briefs.objective: Recognize a low-pressure pocket and choose a controlled carry into it.
briefs.context: Defensive-zone carrier with pressure on one side and a soft middle-side pocket.
briefs.cue: The pocket is open now but closes if the carrier waits.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds soft-area timing; older bank emphasizes pressure and role coverage rather than pocket selection.

briefs.title: Rotate after the wall release
briefs.objective: Choose the next role when a wall carrier releases the puck behind pressure.
briefs.context: Offensive-zone wall cycle with a high player, low player and defender.
briefs.cue: Puck release changes which lane needs support.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds rotation after release; existing cycle-support rotation is a replacement-before-cycle scene.

briefs.title: Change the forecheck angle
briefs.objective: Select an approach that removes the carrier’s preferred outlet while preserving recovery.
briefs.context: Forecheck with a carrier, one outlet and one support defender.
briefs.cue: The carrier’s first outlet is visible and the approach can steer wide.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds outlet-specific angle choice; existing angling research seed is a broad recovery-position comparison.

briefs.title: Reassess the point activation
briefs.objective: Decide whether to activate after checking the covering forward and puck security.
briefs.context: Offensive blue-line player sees a possible activation with explicit cover.
briefs.cue: The puck may be secure or bobbling; cover position changes the choice.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds possession-quality branch; existing defender-activation is a single stated-cover evaluation.

briefs.title: Break the first pressure with a return
briefs.objective: Choose a return pass when the forward lane is closed by a two-player forecheck.
briefs.context: Regroup with defender-to-defender support and two forecheckers shading forward lanes.
briefs.cue: The return lane is open behind the pressure.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds return escape against two-player pressure; existing regroup-under-pressure says hinge without a return-lane comparison.

briefs.title: Receive before choosing the next pass
briefs.objective: Separate a difficult reception from the later tactical choice.
briefs.context: Fast outlet arrives with pressure and two possible next actions.
briefs.cue: The puck may bobble; control is not assumed from proximity.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds possession-quality gate to speed; existing goalie-outlet support assumes released possession.

briefs.title: Use the weak side after pressure
briefs.objective: Recognize a weak-side connection after defenders collapse on the puck.
briefs.context: Offensive-zone carrier with a far-side teammate and one defender overloading.
briefs.cue: Puck-side pressure leaves a visible far-side lane.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds far-side attack under collapse; existing cross-ice support is U13 and half-wall based.

briefs.title: Recover the inside after a wide challenge
briefs.objective: Choose recovery inside after an unsuccessful wide defensive challenge.
briefs.context: Defender challenges wide carrier; a second attacker cuts inside.
briefs.cue: The first challenge misses and the inside threat changes speed.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds failed-wide-challenge recovery; existing backcheck communication is a planned handoff.

briefs.title: Preserve a late-game outlet
briefs.objective: Choose a possession outlet that matches a stated lead-protection objective.
briefs.context: Late-game defensive-zone freeze with a lead and two outlet risks.
briefs.cue: The safer outlet retains possession chance; the aggressive lane is covered.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds late-game objective to outlet selection; existing U18 late-game possession is broader and older-band.

briefs.title: Change jobs after a blocked shot
briefs.objective: Recognize whether to recover or support after an explicitly blocked shot changes possession.
briefs.context: Shot is blocked into a loose puck with both teams transitioning.
briefs.cue: The puck’s new direction and ownership are not assumed from the shooter’s role.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds blocked-shot event transition; existing rebound and transition scenes use saves or clean turnovers.

briefs.title: Choose the clock-aware safe side
briefs.objective: Compare a controlled side-wall hold with a risky central attempt under a stated lead objective.
briefs.context: Late-game lead, score/clock objective explicitly declared; no rules inference.
briefs.cue: The wall lane protects possession while the middle lane is contested.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds side-specific clock management; existing late-game possession compares options without a lane-management detail.

briefs.title: Attack after the penalty kill clears
briefs.objective: Recognize the first attack option after a penalty-kill clear becomes controlled possession.
briefs.context: Scoped special-teams transition from clear to counterattack.
briefs.cue: The puck is secure and the opponent’s unit is changing shape.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds post-clear transition; existing rapid-transition role change uses two turnovers rather than special-teams exit.

briefs.title: Move the penalty kill before the shot
briefs.objective: Choose a rotation that protects the declared high-danger lane before the puck arrives.
briefs.context: Scoped penalty kill with puck moving laterally and a stated protected area.
briefs.cue: The next pass is possible but not yet completed.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds pre-pass anticipation; existing PK backdoor is a post-rotation threat track.

briefs.title: Create a second wave
briefs.objective: Assess a delayed activation after checking possession quality and cover.
briefs.context: Rush entry with first wave pressure and a trailing defender.
briefs.cue: The first wave has control; the covering teammate remains connected.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds delayed second-wave timing; existing defender activation is a generic join decision.

briefs.title: Break the forecheck with a changed exit
briefs.objective: Update the exit when the forechecker takes away the originally planned outlet.
briefs.context: Breakout with two forecheckers and a carrier reading the pressure route.
briefs.cue: The first outlet is removed; a reverse or middle option becomes available.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds multi-cue exit adaptation; existing forecheck-manipulation-regroup focuses on space left by one responsibility change.

briefs.title: Protect the puck through a role exchange
briefs.objective: Choose a support action that keeps possession during a declared role exchange.
briefs.context: Defender rotates low while a forward covers high, with puck under pressure.
briefs.cue: The exchange is called but the puck remains contested.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds possession security to role exchange; existing offensive-role-exchange tests responsibility only.

briefs.title: Read the second defender’s commitment
briefs.objective: Compare pass, carry and shot choices after the second defender commits.
briefs.context: Odd-man attack with both defender and goalie cues shown.
briefs.cue: The second defender’s stick/body position changes the available lane.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds second-defender commitment as the changing cue; existing two-on-one read is an initial options comparison.

briefs.title: Choose the next job after a failed clear
briefs.objective: Update from clear attempt to pressure or coverage after the puck stays in the zone.
briefs.context: Scoped penalty kill where a clear is blocked and possession remains uncertain.
briefs.cue: The puck is loose; the nearest player and high threat are different lanes.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds failed-clear contingency; existing defensive-faceoff contingency begins from a lost draw.

briefs.title: Use the safer first touch under speed
briefs.objective: Choose a first touch that preserves a second option when pressure arrives quickly.
briefs.context: Fast outlet with receiver orientation, pressure and two support lanes visible.
briefs.cue: The preferred touch lane narrows during reception.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds first-touch branching under speed; existing receiving-under-fast-pressure compares prepared play with changed lane but not touch-side options.

briefs.title: Reset the attack after two options vanish
briefs.objective: Recognize when to reset after a shot and pass lane both become covered.
briefs.context: Offensive-zone possession with sequential defender responses and one high reset.
briefs.cue: The first lane is covered, then the second lane closes; possession is still secure.
briefs.noveltyVersusExisting: Adds two-stage conditional reset; existing offensive-possession reset compares one crowded slot with one low option.
